> I couldn't think of much this week, so I decided to go with an RFID safe. It'll have an rfid module, an oled 0.96 inch screen, a 3d printed case, a button, a servo motor for the lock, and it'll all be powered with an arduino UNO. I'm not going to be making a PCB.

## Design

### 2026-11-07: This session was some cad modelling for the safe. It isn't fully done yet and I have some finishing touches to do. This is what I have so far:

**6h**

This session was some cad modelling for the safe. It isn't fully done yet and I have some finishing touches to do. This is what I have so far:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/db453e596ea4231680a646c1bd56a3aa019b2b6f6ff483d4159f353525dfa88b.png)
This took a while because I tried to find 3D models of stuff but it just wasnt working out. They were either waaay too laggy or weren't the right dimensions. I downloaded a bunch of stuff and the only thing that worked was the rfid module.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/ba39f3029c23c9c2079fe1c4ffaa26e5beb47be8572fc0de5e50163bbc1f518e.png)
So about the actual design itself. There are 2 compartments, one is the actual safe and its contents, and one is for the electronics. I am going to be using wires instead of a pcb because those are too complicated, and my PC broke so I'm using a pretty terrible laptop. It has the RFID module that you can use to scan, it'll hold the arduino UNO, and it will connect the servo wires in that small housing. I decided to scrap the OLED and Button because I felt they weren't that necessary and I was running out of time.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/7dd4518360c0850fd884d72e0805b3363b78dda1d6b5e0f81103c03f109b19e3.png)
As you can see there is a little holder for the RFID module, and a small hole for the servo motor. I also measured an rduino UNO to make sure there was enough space. The reason I don't have a hole for the usb port is because I am going to use a 9v battery .

Now this is the actual safe compartment itslef:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/ae9a3278d423a05b4e1e49e294ca0a71277a2be59536fce488e6c162ca8fba25.png)

There is a little holder for the servo motor, and there is a small latch that the servo will use to lock the door. The door is pretty big which is nice. I had to make a servo model myself because I couldnt get one online, this is what I made.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/d926800da16732cbade35de2aff906984d96bcbfc498a05e40bd741f2cdc3443.png)
For some reason the top part of the servo with the little arm is missing. Anyway, the door uses a long cylinder as a  pivot. I made the wall super thick so that the pillar would be thick enough to not snap. It has a diameter of 0.8cm, which I hope is enough.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/81ba23f1f240fe6f6f5bb5e6eec27c66532c3b006e88f88275c4768a6a11b6d5.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/2319534d7b4966523af79819355aba7a16bc50cdb4944ae703e573ad348cadaf.png)
Next, I have to make a schematic for the whole thing, add a detachable roof and some finishing touches, and find some parts.
